findings.title: Device limit enforcement is bypassed after the first rejection due to caching before persistence succeeds
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is executed BEFORE the call to `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)`. When the device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, which TagDevice now propagates and client.go's Authenticate turns into an authentication failure for that request. However, the cache entry for that device ID was already set during this failed attempt. On the very next request from the same (blocked) device, within the ~29 minute cache TTL, tagDeviceUI short-circuits on `a.localCache.Get(key)` and returns nil without ever calling CreateOrUpdateDevice again. TagDevice then returns nil, and Authenticate proceeds to return a valid anonymous Identity. So after the single first rejection, the same over-the-limit device is silently let through for the remainder of the cache TTL, completely defeating the device limit feature for any device that retries (e.g. a browser reload).

findings.title: TOCTOU race between CountDevices and insert allows exceeding the configured device limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first calls CountDevices to check whether the active-device count is >= deviceLimit, and only falls back to updateDevice (reject new devices) when the limit is already reached; otherwise it proceeds with a plain INSERT/UPSERT. There is no transaction, locking, or atomic constraint tying the count check to the subsequent insert. Multiple concurrent requests for different new device IDs can all read a count below the limit and then all insert successfully, letting the active device count exceed deviceLimit. Under any real concurrent anonymous traffic this race defeats the purpose of the configurable device limit.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks synchronously on a DB call with no timeout, removing previous async/timeout/panic-recovery protections
findings.body: Previously TagDevice was invoked in a goroutine with its own context.WithTimeout(2*time.Minute) and a recover() to guard against panics, so a slow or failing device-tagging write never affected the latency or stability of the anonymous authentication response. This change removes the goroutine, the timeout, and the panic recovery, and calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI)` synchronously using the request context. Every anonymous authentication for a not-yet-cached device now blocks on a DB upsert (and, when a device limit is configured, an additional COUNT query) with no bounded timeout of its own, and an unrecovered panic in this path would now propagate into the request-handling goroutine. This is a latency and availability regression on the anonymous auth hot path, especially under DB slowness or load.

findings.title: Changed constructor signature may leave generated DI (Wire) code out of sync
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService's signature changed from accepting `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` (previously resolved elsewhere, presumably via a Wire provider calling anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore) to accepting `sqlStore db.DB` directly and building the AnonDBStore internally with `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)`. anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore's own signature also changed (added deviceLimit int64 parameter). The PR's file list does not include any update to generated wire_gen.go (or equivalent DI wiring) that would reference these constructors; if such generated code exists and still calls the old signatures, the build will fail to compile or Wire codegen will fail due to an unused/missing provider. This should be verified and, if needed, regenerated before merge.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented
findings.body: A new ini key `device_limit` under `[auth.anonymous]` is introduced and parsed into `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, but the PR does not update conf/defaults.ini (sample config) or the configuration documentation to describe this new setting, its default (0 = unlimited), or its effect. Without this, administrators have no way to discover or understand how to configure the new device limit feature.

findings.title: 30-day anonymous-device window duplicated as separate constants across three files
findings.body: The 30-day 'active device' window is now hardcoded independently in three places: `thirtyDays` in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go (used for usage stats), `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go (used for the device-limit count window and the update-match window), and `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go (used for listing devices). These must stay numerically identical for the device-limit feature, usage stats, and the devices API to remain consistent; having three independent literals increases the risk that a future change to one location silently desynchronizes the others.

findings.title: No test coverage for cache-bypass or concurrent device-limit races
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a single new device is rejected once the limit is reached; it does not cover (a) that an already-known device can still refresh its timestamp when the limit is reached, (b) concurrent CreateOrUpdateDevice calls for distinct new devices that could race past the limit (see the CountDevices/insert TOCTOU issue), or (c) the interaction between the local cache in impl.go and repeated calls for a device that was previously rejected, which currently lets a rejected device through on retry. These are exactly the scenarios where the new feature is most likely to fail silently.
